Project Abstract

This mini project is a dual-unit wireless safety system that continuously watches a room for air pollution, carbon monoxide, LPG/smoke leakage, and open flame — then reacts to all four without a single line of code. A transmitter unit reads four sensors, checks each against a threshold using analog comparators, and radios an alert to a receiver unit up to several metres away over a 433 MHz link.

The receiver decodes the alert, lights matching status LEDs, sounds a remote buzzer, and switches a relay-driven 5V exhaust fan on automatically — ventilating the space before the hazard escalates. Every stage, from sensing to wireless encoding to fan control, is built entirely from discrete sensors and off-the-shelf logic ICs, making the whole system reproducible without any microcontroller programming.

System Architecture

click any component for details

Transmitter Unit

  • MQ-135 Air Quality SensorSenses smog and general air pollutants (NH₃, benzene, CO₂ family gases).
  • MQ-7 CO SensorDetects carbon monoxide concentration — an early warning for combustion leaks.
  • MQ-2 Smoke / LPG SensorPicks up smoke particles and LPG gas leakage.
  • Flame SensorIR-based module that triggers on the light signature of an open flame.
  • LM358 ComparatorCompares each analog sensor voltage against a potentiometer-set threshold.
  • 10-Segment LED Bar GraphGives a live, local reading of pollution / danger level (1–10).
  • HT12E Encoder ICConverts the triggered comparator outputs into a serial code for RF transmission.
  • 433 MHz RF TransmitterBroadcasts the encoded alert wirelessly to the receiver unit.
  • Local Buzzer + Safe/Warning/Danger/Fire LEDsImmediate on-site audible and visual alarm.
433 MHz
WIRELESS
LINK

Receiver Unit

  • 433 MHz RF ReceiverPicks up the wireless alert sent from the transmitter unit.
  • HT12D Decoder ICDecodes the incoming serial data back into parallel alert outputs.
  • Danger / Warning / Fire LEDsRemote visual status matching the condition detected at the transmitter.
  • Buzzer (Remote Alarm)Sounds at the receiver end so the alert is heard away from the source.
  • 5V Relay ModuleSwitches the higher-current exhaust fan load using the low-current decoder signal.
  • 5V USB Exhaust FanAutomatically switches on to ventilate the area the moment a hazard is confirmed.

How It Works

signal path, sensor → fan
01

Continuous Monitoring

MQ-135, MQ-7, MQ-2 and the flame sensor constantly sample the surrounding air and light conditions.

02

Threshold Comparison

The LM358 comparator checks each sensor's output against a preset trip point.

03

Local Alert & Encoding

A crossed threshold lights the LED bar graph, sounds the local buzzer, and is packaged by the HT12E encoder.

04

Wireless Response

The 433 MHz link carries the alert to the receiver, which decodes it, lights remote LEDs, sounds the buzzer, and switches on the exhaust fan via the relay.

06

LED Indications

transmitter unit status colours
Green — Safe
Yellow — Warning
Red — Danger
Red (fast) — Fire Detected
07

Features

  • Detects air pollution, CO gas, smoke/LPG, and fire in one unit
  • 10-segment LED bar graph for real-time pollution level
  • Local and remote buzzer alarms
  • Fully wireless alert over 433 MHz RF — no wiring between rooms
  • Automatic exhaust fan ON/OFF via relay
  • Runs entirely off a portable 5V power bank
  • Built with encoder/decoder ICs — no Arduino, no programming
